q: 1. For the construction of the retaining structures, the type of concrete mix to be used, is
explain: For retaining structures which require higher strength due to lateral earth pressures, a richer mix of 1:1½:3 (M20 grade) is typically used.

q: 2. The correct proportion of ingredients of concrete, depends upon
explain: Correct mix proportioning must account for all these factors - bulking of sand, water content, absorption of aggregates, and desired workability - to achieve an accurate and effective concrete mix.

q: 3. The following proportion of the ingredients or concrete mix, is not in confirmation to arbitrary method of proportioning
explain: In the arbitrary method, the standard nominal mixes follow ratios like 1:1:2, 1:2:4, 1:3:6, 1:4:8; the ratio 1:4:10 does not fit this standard arbitrary series.

q: 4. The bond strength between steel and concrete is due to
explain: The bond between reinforcing steel and surrounding concrete develops through a combination of both frictional resistance and adhesive chemical bonding at the interface.

q: 5. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following
options: workability of the concrete mix decreases with an increase in the moisture content
concrete for which preliminary tests are conducted, is called controlled concrete
bulking of sand depends upon the finesse of grains
concrete mix 1:6:12, is used for mass concrete in piers
explain: Workability actually increases (not decreases) with an increase in moisture content up to a point, since more water makes the mix more fluid and easier to work with, making this the incorrect statement.

q: 6. The concrete shrinkage is more pronounced in
explain: A rich mix contains a higher proportion of cement paste (which is the shrinking component), so shrinkage is more pronounced in rich mixes compared to lean mixes.

q: 7. Poisson's ratio of concrete reduced by using
explain: Using a richer mix (more cement content) tends to reduce the Poisson's ratio of the resulting concrete.

q: 8. For finding compressive strength of concrete, the minimum number of cubes required is
explain: As per standard testing practice, a minimum of 3 concrete cubes are cast and tested to determine the average compressive strength for a given sample.

q: 9. The 28 days cube strength of mass concrete using aggregates of maximum size 5 cm for gravity dams should be
explain: For mass concrete in gravity dams using large aggregate (5 cm max size), the required 28-day cube strength is relatively modest, typically specified as below 200 kg/cm², since strength requirements are lower than structural concrete.

q: 10. The behavior of concrete under instantaneous loads is
explain: Under instantaneous (short-duration) loading, concrete behaves approximately as an elastic material, following a near-linear stress-strain relationship.

q: 11. The durability of concrete is due to its resistance to
explain: Durability of concrete is defined by its overall ability to resist deterioration from a combination of environmental exposure, internal disruptive forces, and chemical attack/cracking.

q: 12. Concrete can take tension up to
options: 10% of the compressive strength of steel
10% of the combined compressive strength of concrete & R/F
10% of the total tensile strength of the section
explain: Concrete's tensile strength is generally only about 10% of its own compressive strength, reflecting its characteristic weakness in tension relative to compression.

q: 13. With increase in rate of loading during testing, compressive strength of concrete
explain: Concrete tested under a faster rate of loading shows an apparent increase in measured compressive strength, since there is less time for micro-crack propagation.

q: 14. The ratio of various ingredients (cement, sand, aggregates) in concrete of grade M 200, is
explain: The nominal mix proportion associated with grade M200 concrete (equivalent to M20 in modern notation) is 1 : 1.5 : 3 (cement : sand : coarse aggregate).

q: 15. The cube strength of concrete exceeds the cylinder strength by (in percent)
explain: Due to the difference in specimen geometry and the resulting confinement/end effects during testing, cube strength typically exceeds cylinder strength by about 20 to 25%.

q: 16. For cylindrical specimens, the dimension of cylinder generally used
explain: The standard cylindrical test specimen used for compressive strength testing has a diameter of 15 cm and a height of 30 cm, giving the standard height-to-diameter ratio of 2.

q: 17. Cube test is used to determine
explain: The standard cube test is specifically designed to determine the compressive strength of concrete, the most commonly required strength parameter.

q: 18. For cylindrical specimens, minimum strength required should be
options: 0.20 times the strength of 15 cm cubes
0.40 times the strength of 15 cm cubes
0.60 times the strength of 15 cm cubes
0.80 times the strength of 15 cm cubes
explain: The compressive strength obtained from a standard cylinder is typically about 0.80 times the strength of an equivalent 15 cm cube, due to the difference in specimen shape and testing conditions.

q: 19. The surface area of standard cube used for finding compressive strength of concrete is
explain: The standard cube face is 15cm x 15cm = 225 cm² = 22500 mm² = 0.0225 m² - all these are equivalent expressions of the same area in different units, so all of the above is correct.

q: 20. During application of load on cylindrical specimen the failure plane makes an angle of .........with the horizontal.
explain: Under compressive load, cylindrical concrete specimens typically fail along a shear plane inclined at approximately 60 degrees to the horizontal (or about 30 degrees to the vertical axis of loading).

q: 21. The ultimate load of a balanced reinforced concrete beam is proportional to
options: crushing strength of concrete and/or tensile strength of the steel
explain: In a balanced section, both the concrete's crushing (compressive) strength and the steel's tensile strength reach their limiting values simultaneously, so the ultimate load depends on both.

q: 22. The grade of concrete M 150 means that compressive strength of 15 cm cube after 28 days is
explain: By definition, the grade designation M150 directly specifies a characteristic compressive strength of 150 kg/cm² for a 15cm cube tested after 28 days.

q: 23. The test conducted in the labouratory on the specimen made out of trial concrete mix is called
explain: A preliminary test is carried out in the laboratory on specimens made from trial concrete mixes to establish suitable proportions before actual construction begins.

q: 24. Allowable shear strength of concrete, depends upon
explain: The allowable shear strength of concrete is generally derived as a function of, and depends upon, its compressive strength, as per design code provisions.

q: 25. The strength of concrete is decreased by
explain: Excessive vibration (over-vibration), impact loading, and fatigue (repeated cyclic loading) can all contribute to a decrease in the effective strength of concrete over time.

q: 26. The most appropriate method to specify the concrete mix is by
explain: Specifying concrete by its grade (e.g., M20, M25) is considered the most appropriate and standardized method, as it directly denotes the required characteristic compressive strength.

q: 27. The total number of grades of ordinary concrete stipulated in IS 456:2000 are
explain: IS 456:2000 stipulates a total of 6 grades under the ordinary concrete category (M10, M15, M20, M25, M30... within the ordinary grade group).

q: 28. The standard size of a concrete cube for compressive strength test is
explain: The standard concrete cube specimen size used for compressive strength testing is 150 mm x 150 mm x 150 mm (15 cm cube).

q: 29. If the various concrete ingredients i.e. cement, sand and aggregates are in the ratio of 1:3:6, the grade of concrete, is
explain: The nominal mix ratio 1:3:6 corresponds to the M150 grade of concrete as per standard grade-mix ratio correlations.

q: 30. Permissible compressive strength of M150 concrete grade is
explain: As indicated by its designation, the M150 grade of concrete has a characteristic (permissible) compressive strength of 150 kg/cm².

q: 31. Permissible compressive strength of M150 concrete grade is
explain: 150 kg/cm² is equivalent to approximately 15 N/mm² (since 1 N/mm² ≈ 10.2 kg/cm²), making 15 N/mm² the correct equivalent expression of the M150 grade strength.

q: 32. Permissible compressive strength of M200 concrete grade is
explain: By definition, the M200 grade concrete has a characteristic (permissible) compressive strength of 200 kg/cm².

q: 33. The ratio of various ingredients (cement, sand, aggregates) in concrete of grade M 200, is
explain: The M200 grade of concrete typically corresponds to a nominal mix ratio of 1:1.5:3 (cement:sand:aggregate).

q: 34. Permissible compressive strength of M250 concrete grade is
explain: By definition, the M250 grade concrete has a characteristic (permissible) compressive strength of 250 kg/cm².

q: 35. Permissible compressive strength of M300 concrete grade is
explain: By definition, the M300 grade concrete has a characteristic (permissible) compressive strength of 300 kg/cm².

q: 36. The concrete mixes are designated into
explain: As per the classification used in this text (older IS 456 provisions), concrete mixes are designated into seven standard grades.

q: 37. Which of the following grade is not recommended by IS 456:1978
explain: M55 grade is not among the standard grades listed/recommended under the (older) IS 456:1978 provisions referenced in this text.

q: 38. The test conducted in the laboratory on the specimen made out of trial concrete mix is called
explain: A preliminary test is a laboratory test performed on trial mix specimens to determine and finalize the mix design before actual site work begins.

q: 39. In preliminary test, the concrete is placed in the mould in ......... layers of equal volume.
explain: As per standard cube/cylinder casting procedure for preliminary tests, concrete is placed and compacted in three equal layers.

q: 40. The preliminary test should be repeated if the difference of compressive strength of three test specimen exceeds.
explain: As per the acceptance criteria in this text, if the compressive strength results of the three test specimens vary by more than 1.5 N/mm², the preliminary test must be repeated.

q: 41. The factors which affects the design of concrete mix is
explain: Concrete mix design is influenced jointly by aggregate fineness modulus, water-cement ratio, and required workability (slump) — hence all of these factors are relevant.

q: 42. For the construction of RCC slab, column, beam and walls, the minimum grade of concrete mixed is used for
explain: The minimum recommended nominal mix for general RCC construction (slabs, columns, beams, walls) is 1:2:4, corresponding to M15 grade concrete.

q: 43. M100 grade of concrete approximates
explain: The M100 grade of concrete (lowest strength grade) approximately corresponds to a lean nominal mix ratio of 1:3:6.

q: 44. The number of bags of cement required per cubic meter of 1:2:4 concrete will be approximately
explain: For a nominal 1:2:4 concrete mix, standard calculations show that approximately 4 to 5 bags of cement (50 kg each) are needed per cubic metre of concrete.

q: 45. M150 grade of concrete approximates
explain: The M150 grade of concrete approximately corresponds to a nominal mix ratio of 1:2:4 (cement:sand:aggregate).

q: 46. Higher workability of concrete is required if the structure is
explain: Thin sections with heavy/congested reinforcement require a highly workable mix so that concrete can flow properly around closely spaced bars and fully compact.

q: 47. To determine modulus of rupture, the size of test specimen used is
explain: As per IS 516, the standard flexural (modulus of rupture) test beam specimen size is 150 × 150 × 700 mm.

q: 48. Workability of concrete is directly proportional to
explain: Well-graded aggregate reduces void content and improves the flow characteristics of the mix, thereby directly improving workability.

q: 49. Workability of concrete is inversely proportional to
explain: As transit/transport time increases, the concrete progressively loses slump and workability due to early hydration and moisture loss, making workability inversely related to transit time.

q: 50. Approximate value of shrinkage strain in concrete
explain: The typical order of magnitude for drying shrinkage strain in ordinary concrete is about 0.0003 (i.e., 3×10⁻⁴).
